To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

acanthocyte-positive red blood cells in NA/NBIA patients show a decreased response in drug-induced membrane endocytosis (vesicles) and calcium uptake upon stimulation with lysophosphatic acid, compared to acanthocyte-negative red blood cells in the same patient group and to healthy red blood cells.

1) acanthocytes show a reduced response in several functional tests, 2) the acanthocytotic state is not restricted to ChAc and can be found also in acanthocyte positive NBIA (PKNA) red cells, 3) the acanthocytes from ChAc patients show a reduced response, which can be restored by incubation with the cholesterol-uptake blocker MβCD.

ChAc acanthocytic RBCs show a reduced response in endovesiculation and lysophosphatydilic acid-induced PS exposure and calcium uptake, suggesting that acanthocytic cells may be in an “acanthocyte state”, and this state may be associated with a neurodegenerative process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the red cell membrane in the context of the NA/NBIA diseases and its possible role as a model for understanding the pathological pathways of neurodegeneration in general.
the identification and functional analysis of the molecular basis of red blood cell alterations in NA/NBIA.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of neuroacanthocytoses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
acanthocytoses are not a mere side effect of NA/NBIA but rather a consequence of a more complex pathophysiological process.
the red blood cells in NA/NBIA patients are not only a marker of the disease, but may also play an important role in the development of the neurodegenerative process.
acanthocytoses are a common finding in neurodegenerative disorders and that the acanthocytotic red cells may be an indicator of the neurodegenerative state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the acanthocytes in NA and PKAN patients are not just a mere morphological change, but rather represent a functional state of the red cell membrane.
acanthocytic cells are less sensitive to stimuli that cause membrane remodeling and that this is due to a change in membrane properties that may be related to the disease.
the acanthocyte is a cell that has a reduced capacity to respond to stimuli, and this reduced capacity is a result of changes in the lipid composition of the cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
acanthocytic shape and impaired functionality are linked.
acanthocyte formation in NA/NBIA patients is associated with a functional alteration of red cell membrane properties.
the acanthocytotic shape is associated with altered membrane properties.
